subtitle: Turning raw billing and usage data into trusted marts

caption: Driftwood's driftwood_analytics project follows this same staging / intermediate / marts layering, browsable in the dbt IDE.
A real dbt run output -- every model built in order, the same sequence Driftwood's own staging-to-marts chain follows.

eyebrow: Staging: clean and rename, nothing clever
code:
-- stg_billing_events.sql
select subscriber_id, event_type,
  try_to_decimal(amount_usd,10,2) as amount_usd
from {{ source('driftwood_raw','billing_events') }}

-- stg_usage_events.sql
select user_id as subscriber_id,  -- renamed here, once
  watch_duration_seconds
from {{ source('driftwood_raw','usage_events') }}
caption: The user_id -> subscriber_id rename happens once, in staging -- never in marts or Power BI.

code:
-- int_subscriber_activity.sql
select b.subscriber_id, b.event_type, b.amount_usd,
  sum(u.watch_duration_seconds) as watch_seconds
from {{ ref('stg_billing_events') }} b
left join {{ ref('stg_usage_events') }} u
  on b.subscriber_id = u.subscriber_id
caption: ref(), not a hardcoded table name -- this is what builds dbt's dependency graph automatically.

eyebrow: Every ref() becomes a real lineage graph
caption: dbt's own lineage graph, generated automatically from ref() calls -- the exact dependency chain Driftwood's layering produces.

eyebrow: Marts: what Power BI actually queries
code:
-- fct_subscriptions.sql (fact: one row per event)
select subscriber_id, event_type, amount_usd
from {{ ref('int_subscriber_activity') }}

-- dim_subscribers.sql (dimension: one row per subscriber)
select subscriber_id, min(event_timestamp) as first_seen_at
from {{ ref('int_subscriber_activity') }} group by 1
caption: Fact and dimension -- the same split the dbt and Power BI courses both already taught.
